dataset_family: Iran Dementia and Alzheimer's Association (IDAA, Tehran) Kinect gait sample, 70 MCI / 80 HC
method_family: Kinect V2 skeletal gait features (single-task, dual-task, dual-task cost) + hierarchical ANFIS classifier (vs LR and SVM)
what_it_shows: Kinect V2 dual-task gait with a hierarchical ANFIS classified 70 MCI vs 80 HC at a reported 93% accuracy (90% sensitivity, 91.5% F-score). On the same features LR reached 81.25% and SVM 78.85%. Single-task gait gave 86.87%. The paper states no validation scheme for the ANFIS figures.
why: PDF IDENTITY. The P-114 map entry (1-s2.0-S1746809421000963) is the wrong paper: San-Martin et al., an EEG/LORETA study, BSPC 66:102499. The block's own file name (S1746809421003195) is not in downloads/. The paper the block describes is the file the map assigns to P-115: 1-s2.0-S1746809421007928-main.pdf (Seifallahi et al., BSPC 71 (2022) 103195, doi 10.1016/j.bspc.2021.103195). Its content matches the block on every point: Kinect V2 skeletal gait, ANFIS, 70 MCI/80 HC, 26 features, STW/DTW/DTC, 93%. The verdict rests on that file, read in full to the References. The map needs repair: P-114 -> S1746809421007928; P-115's block names S1746809422004092. AGAINST TABLE A1. (a) Consumer-grade hardware: yes. The device is a Microsoft Kinect V2 depth camera on a tripod, which the authors contrast with GAITRite and body-worn sensors. (b) Behavioural instrument: yes (gait). (c) High standalone accuracy: yes, as reported. ANFIS reaches 93% with all 26 DTW features, 88.12% with the 11 selected DTW features and 86.87% on single-task walking (Tables 5-6). (d) No head-to-head against a specialist instrument: consistent with the statement's caveat. The only comparison is ANFIS against LR/SVM on the same features. (e) Self-administered: fails. Recorders instruct the participants, who practise the walks several times, and the capture is run from a MATLAB GUI on a connected computer. VALIDATION WEAKNESS. The paper states no train/test split or cross-validation for the ANFIS figures. Its only validation statement is five-fold CV 'of training data' for SVM hyperparameter tuning. The discussion says only that the classifiers 'were trained and tested using each set of databases separately'. The 93% therefore cannot be confirmed as a held-out figure. Derived arithmetic: several reported accuracies (e.g. 86.87%, 74.81%, 76.33%) are not multiples of 1/150, which suggests averaging over partitions the paper does not report. MCI labelling is loosely described: MMSE/MoCA questionnaires plus unspecified 'neurological, psychological, and physical diagnosis tests', with amnestic and non-amnestic MCI pooled. AGAINST THE NARROWED WORDING. It fits 'low-cost behavioural data captured without specialist hardware', and its best-case standalone accuracy (93%) lies in the ~88-94% band. 'Internally validated' is not demonstrated, because the validation scheme behind the 93% is not printed. Verdict: partly. If the operator accepts an unstated validation scheme, this is the closest of the four candidates to the narrowed form. INDEPENDENCE. The sample was recruited in Iran through the IDAA in Tehran. That is a distinct dataset and method family from I-CONECT facial video (P-76/P-77) and from Memory Guard (P-101). No authors are shared with the supporters or with the other candidates. Outside the supporter set: P-1082 (Seifallahi, Galvin, Ghoraani; Kinect v2 curve walking; IDAA; 30 HC/25 MCI; no accuracy reported) shares the lead author, the device and the recruiting organisation. Participant overlap with P-1082 is possible but unverified. P-1082 is neither a supporter nor a candidate. The P-114 registry row (Behavioural/digital, N 150) matches this paper.

quotes.quote: Generally, the proposed ANFIS classifier had values of 93%, 90%, and 91.5% for accuracy, sensitivity, and F-score, respectively when all extracted gait parameters in the DTW condition for the classification of elderly subjects to MCI and HC groups.
The study included 70 elders with MCI and 80 healthy control (HC) elderly subjects who were selected based on specific criteria.
A KinectV.2 camera was mounted on a tripod with a suitable distance from the oval path which was approximately 10 m long
The Kinect camera was connected to a computer, and the recording process was controlled using a graphical user interface (GUI) designed in MATLAB2017.
Before recording gait tests, enough information about the tests was given to the subjects by recorders.
The MCI subjects of the present study were selected through clients of the Iran dementia and Alzheimer’s Association (IDAA) in Tehran city of Iran after the necessary diagnosis and checkup tests
[p.7: Considering the accuracy metric, the ANFIS, LR, and SVM showed] the values of 93%, 81.25%, and 78.85%, respectively when the whole collection of DTW features were used for classification.
The accuracy of ANFIS, LR, and SVM were 88.12%, 75%, and 73.75%, respectively when just selected gait parameters of DTW were utilized for classification.
[SVM gamma and C were selected] based on the five-fold validation of training data.
three various gait feature collections called STW, DTW, and DTC were as databases where the classifiers were trained and tested using each set of databases separately.

The skeletal data of elders’ bodies were recorded during various walking tets with Kinect V.2 camera of Microsoft instead of implementing the usual previous gait analyzing systems with pressure sensors e.g. GAITRite or systems with accelerometer and gyroscope
all individuals with two different types of a-MCI and na-MCI were considered as a single group as individuals with MCI.
